0.long_answer: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a betaherpesvirus that is part of the TORCH group of vertically transmitted infections. CMV can be transmitted from mother to fetus during pregnancy, and it is the most common viral cause of congenital infection. Infection during pregnancy can lead to a range of serious complications in newborns, including sensorineural hearing loss (deafness), as well as other neurological impairments. Its ability to cause congenital infection and subsequent developmental issues makes it a significant concern in prenatal care.
